shots.focal_element: Notion AI prompt input box in the right-hand agent panel, with the text being typed into it
on_screen_text: How can I help you today?
Create a bug tracking dashboard...populate with feedback from Slack and Notion and my emails.
shots.typography: Product UI sans-serif (likely Notion's Inter-style UI face, low confidence); semibold sentence-case panel heading, regular-weight sentence-case menu items and prompt text, normal tracking; tiny blue 'New' pill badge.
shots.what_happens: Cropped close-up of the Notion AI side panel (mascot avatar with hat, greeting, three suggestion rows) framed against a blue backdrop; the prompt is typed on character by character with a blinking caret, the line already starting mid-sentence with an ellipsis jump ('dashboard...populate'), then the cursor moves to and clicks the blue send button around 31 s. The very last sampled frame (0:32.000) already shows the next 'Thinking' screen, so the shot boundary is within a frame of it.
shots.build_rebuild: Render a static recreation of the agent panel cropped to the right two-thirds over a solid blue backdrop, animate the prompt string with a per-character typewriter (about 15-20 chars/s, skipping the middle via an ellipsis) plus blinking caret, then tween a cursor onto the send button and play a press state.

shots.focal_element: Notion AI mascot avatar in a white circle beside the status word with three coloured loading dots
shots.typography: Large regular-to-medium weight sans-serif in title case, normal tracking, black on off-white; followed by three small coloured dots acting as an ellipsis.
shots.what_happens: Full-frame interstitial on an off-white background: the mascot face with cowboy hat sits beside 'Thinking' with animated dots; around 33.5 s the face swaps to a scribbled pen-stroke drawing and the label changes to 'Crafting', signalling the agent moving from reasoning to building.
shots.build_rebuild: Center a circular avatar with soft drop shadow next to a large label on an off-white canvas, loop three coloured dots in a staggered bounce, and at the state change crossfade the avatar illustration and swap the label text from 'Thinking' to 'Crafting'.

shots.composition_other: Starts as a centered app window on a blue backdrop, then the virtual camera pushes in and reframes onto the right-hand agent chat column, then pulls back out to the full window.
shots.focal_element: The Bug Tracking Dashboard page being generated on the left while the agent's reasoning and search results stream into the right-hand chat panel
on_screen_text: Log new bugs directly below or paste links to messages, issues, or emails
Keep Status and Priority up to date
I'll compile a concise list of each bug along with links to the specific Slack messages. I think that'll be clear and useful!
shots.typography: Product UI sans-serif (Inter-like, low confidence): bold large title-case page heading with bug emoji, bold sentence-case section heads, regular body bullets; small grey regular text for agent status lines; truncated Slack message rows with light-grey channel labels.
shots.what_happens: The full Notion window shows the new 'Bug Tracking Dashboard' page building itself (heading, how-to bullets, empty Bug Tracker table with view tabs) while the page scrolls up; the camera then pushes into the agent panel where 'Compiling bug reports' text streams in and a 'Searched for "bug reports"' card appears with source tabs (Notion, Slack, Notion Mail) whose result counters tick upward (7 to 62 results) and Slack message rows stack in; 'Updating database...' appears, the camera pulls back to the full window and the table fills row by row with bugs, status pills and priority tags. The final sampled frame (0:45.000) already shows the next 'What can I wrangle up for ya?' screen.
shots.build_rebuild: Build a static app-window mock on a blue backdrop, scroll the page content up as table rows mask-in, keyframe a camera scale/translate push into the chat column while streaming text word by word and counting result numbers up, then ease the camera back out and stagger-reveal table rows with their status and priority pills.

shots.focal_element: Isolated, enlarged prompt input box with the follow-up instruction being typed
on_screen_text: What can I wrangle up for ya?
shots.typography: Semibold sentence-case sans-serif greeting beside the mascot avatar; regular-weight prompt text with a caret; small grey regular context-chip label; normal tracking throughout.
shots.what_happens: On a plain off-white canvas, the mascot greets with a playful 'What can I wrangle up for ya?' above a blue-outlined prompt box scoped to the Bug Tracking Dashboard; the follow-up '...and assign the appropriate engineers' types on, the cursor clicks send at about 47.5 s, and the last sampled frame (0:48.500) already shows the next full-window shot.
shots.build_rebuild: Center a scaled-up prompt component with a context chip on an off-white background, typewriter the instruction with a caret at roughly 12-15 chars/s, then move a cursor onto the round blue send button and trigger a press state before cutting.

shots.focal_element: Bug Tracker table with a new Assignee column appearing, plus the agent status line in the side panel
on_screen_text: Log new bugs directly below or paste links to messages, issues, or emails
Keep Status and Priority up to date
shots.typography: Product UI sans-serif (Inter-like, low confidence): bold title-case table heading, regular sentence-case bullets and row titles, small rounded status pills and P0-P2 priority tags, small grey agent status lines.
shots.what_happens: Back to the full app window on blue: the populated bug table is shown with the follow-up message now in the chat panel; within about a second an empty 'Assignee' column is inserted between Bug and Status and the agent status changes from 'Updating database...' to 'Adding engineers...'.
shots.build_rebuild: Show the window mock with the filled table, then animate a new column sliding in by widening the gap between the Bug and Status columns while swapping the side-panel status text from 'Updating database...' to 'Adding engineers...'.
